turn.summary: Read-only external landscape research (web searches over byte-level architectures, stateful agent platforms, multi-agent debate, lifelong-learning memory, blackboard/transaction patterns, scaling-law economics, and the personal-AI product space). No code, State, doctrine, or training touched; Kimmy's C1 campaign was not disturbed. Key findings delivered to Jeff: (1) Byte Latent Transformer (Meta, ACL 2025) validates tokenizer-free byte-level modeling at 8B scale and shows robustness/long-tail gains - partial validation of Axon's no-tokenizer stance - but uses learned entropy-based dynamic patching, far more adaptive than Axon's frozen fixed 16D cells. (2) Letta/MemGPT is the closest commercial analog for stateful agents (persistent memory, sleep-time compute, self-editing memory blocks) but its memory is LLM-managed text/embeddings, not exact provenance-bound canonical state under a deterministic transaction authority. (3) MIT multi-agent debate research validates the society-of-cores direction; Network-AI (TS orchestrator) independently implements propose->validate->commit blackboard locking, showing the governance pattern has recognized value - but as a wrapper around model calls, not as an organism's canonical state identity.
